title: The first to believe
hookLine: Khadijah first, then Ali, Zayd and Abu Bakr

cards: Arise and warn, the verse said. Yet the first believers weren't found in a crowd: not in the marketplace, not among the chiefs of Quraysh by the Ka'ba.

They were the people who shared his meals: a wife, a young cousin, a freed man who lived under the same roof. And one friend from outside the house, a merchant he had known for years. The message began at home.

teach.b: Ibn Ishaq, the early biographer, gives the order as the sirah tradition remembers it. Khadijah first, before anyone else: the woman who had heard the whole story that first night believed what he told her.
Then Ali, his young cousin, who had grown up in that house; Ibn Ishaq tells of Ali coming upon the Prophet and Khadijah praying together and asking what it was.
Then Zayd ibn Harithah, the freed man who had chosen to stay. Then Abu Bakr, a merchant friend from outside the household.
Sources differ about who came first among the men, and some later scholars settle it gently, giving each a place: the first woman, the first youth, the first freed man, the first free man.
Nobody had to lose so someone else could win. And look at who they are: a wife, a cousin raised as a son, a former slave, an old friend. Not one of them needed a miracle from a stranger.
They knew him. They had watched him keep his word, and seen him settle the quarrel over the black stone so every clan held an edge of the cloak.
When he said something had happened in the cave, they weighed it against years of what he was.
In surah nine, verse one hundred, the Qur'an speaks of as-sabiqun al-awwalun, the first forerunners among the emigrants and the helpers, and says Allah is well pleased with them.
Commentators differ over exactly whom the verse means, and some sirah teachers borrow its phrase for these earliest names.
Belief, in this story, starts close to home, in the people who had seen the most of an ordinary life.

how: In sirah study, Muslims learn the names of the earliest believers, beginning with Khadijah, and remember them with honor.

games.q: you've just heard the message in the cave. who do you tell first?
o: the people in your own house.
games.why: the first to believe were his household and one close friend: Khadijah, Ali, Zayd, then Abu Bakr.

practice: Go back to some beginning, a new job, a first song, an idea nobody else liked, and ask who said yes first.

Recall the exact words they used, or the small thing they did, as closely as you can, and shape one sentence of thanks around it, to say someday, or in your heart if they're gone. If you pray, ask good for them.

wordCard.voice: Zayd. The freed man who had chosen to stay with the Prophet's household, and who believed soon after Khadijah and Ali. Today's word.
